clue.text: Coolness exhibited by father about to see doctor

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
lo is an old word meaning look or see
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A father calmly reverses course before visiting his doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here signals a turnaround, not a container round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe composure and self-assurance under pressure.

clue.text: Music that's still heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: stillness or quiet is peace

explanation.surface: Music that can still be heard after it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is a noun here, calm or quiet, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single musical composition.

clue.text: Decree — one circumvented by government department

indicators.note: circumvented means surrounded, so the department goes around the numeral

parts.note: the Ordnance, as in the Board of Ordnance or Ordnance Survey, is a government department
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A decree gets around a Whitehall department.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's official mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative order or regulation.

clue.text: Note in plainsong

indicators.note: in places the note inside the word for plain

parts.note: bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note in a piece of church chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plainsong' must be split: 'plain' gives BALD and 'song' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a simple narrative song.

clue.text: Cunning and skill provided diamonds

parts.note: art can mean skill or craft
if means provided that
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jewel thief brings cunning and skill, provided there are diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is trickery or craft, the noun for cunning.

clue.text: Berlin's call to arms

parts.note: Irving Berlin's musical about a sharpshooter, whose title is an urging to take up a weapon

explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote the musical about sharpshooter Annie Oakley, and its title urges her to take up arms.

clue.text: Possible end to joint holiday in Bangkok, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the phrase is spoken and heard as a similar-sounding one

parts.note: a break in Thailand, whose capital is Bangkok, is a Thai break

explanation.surface: A trip to Thailand might end a shared arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' means tied, level: a tennis set at six all ends in a tiebreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreak decides a contest when the players are level.

clue.text: Place to discuss raising of spirits

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A venue for talking about the lifting of morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' suits a down clue, where the reversed word reads upwards; 'spirits' is drink, not morale.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting place or medium for open debate.

clue.text: Some lines were initially cost-free — that's changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters are to be rearranged
initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Wrinkles once came at no charge, but no longer.
explanation.walkthrough: W, the first letter of 'were', joins COSTFREE and the nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the fine wrinkles at the outer corners of the eyes.

clue.text: Cleared fen out, discovering a venomous creature

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clearing out a marsh comes across a poisonous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CLEAREDFEN, signalled by 'out', gives the snake; the file's text read 'ten' where the page prints 'fen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fer-de-lance is a highly poisonous pit viper of tropical America.

clue.text: Bird that moves in a straight line

definitions.text: that moves in a straight line

explanation.surface: A crow that flies as the crow flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook is a black crow-family bird, and also the chess piece that travels only along ranks and files.

clue.text: Busy again polling a tree

indicators.note: to poll a tree is to cut off its top, so the first letter is lopped off

parts.note: a greengage is a kind of plum tree

explanation.surface: Someone busy again, pruning a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Polling a tree means cutting its head back, so GREENGAGE loses its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-engage is to become occupied or involved once more.

clue.text: Careless of what follows do saints…

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale do is followed by re and mi

explanation.surface: An unfinished remark about what saints do next, careless of the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next ones as a running sentence, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duty.

clue.text: …shock, being crazy about…

indicators.note: about tells us the word for crazy is turned round

parts.note: nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Part of a running sentence: saints shocked at being thought mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or stupefy.

clue.text: Stars need help, perhaps, in difficult setting

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for difficult

parts.note: tough means difficult

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Celebrities need assistance on a tricky film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the anagram of 'help' and 'in' puts it inside; 'need' and 'setting' are surface padding. The Plough is the British name for the Big Dipper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plough is a group of seven bright stars in Ursa Major.

clue.text: …inspector, formerly an underground worker?

parts.note: ex means former or formerly
a miner works below ground

explanation.surface: An inspector who used to dig coal underground.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is someone who inspects or tests.

clue.text: Unfortunate — that's covering girl upset over man

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first part above the next
covering means the letters for that's go around the next piece

parts.note: i.e. stands for that is

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: moll is a slang word for a girl
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: A gloomy tale of a girl upset over a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals a reversal in a down clue, 'covering' a container, and 'over' puts the man's name below.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-omened means doomed or ill-starred.

clue.text: Diaphanous rags, some in tatters .

indicators.note: in tatters suggests the words are torn up and their letters reassembled

parts.note: the letters of these words are the material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Flimsy clothing, some of it torn to shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is light, sheer fabric, so the adjective means very fine and see-through.

clue.text: Form in which rabbit-like creature hides before noon

indicators.note: the creature hides the other letters, holding them inside it

parts.note: a cony is a rabbit, or the rabbit-like hyrax
ere is an old word for before
M stands for meridies, noon, as in a.m. and p.m.

explanation.surface: A rabbit hiding in its burrow until midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' is the container signal; 'in which' merely links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony is a set form or ritual of proceedings.

clue.text: Only the front portions of Los Angeles train eventually departed

indicators.note: only the front portions means keep just the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles train finally leaves after a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean dead, as in the late king, a euphemism for departed.

clue.text: Stout is alcoholic

explanation.surface: A dark beer with a kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong means sturdy or robust, and also with a high alcohol content.

clue.text: Pants, and becomes slower

explanation.surface: Someone out of breath slows down.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are casual trousers (pants in American usage); slacks as a verb means eases off or slows.

clue.text: Inferior headgear man's wearing

indicators.note: the man is wearing the headgear, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
he is a male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: A shoddy hat on a man's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap can mean shoddy or of poor quality.

clue.text: Amulet it could be most important

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A lucky charm may be the most important thing you own.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means fundamental or paramount, the most basic or important.

clue.text: Sample some of Malta's temptations

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Try a few of the Mediterranean island's delights.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample is to try a little, as when one tries food.

clue.text: Contemptible character acquires cigarette-end to smoke

parts.note: a cur is a worthless, despicable person
the end of the word cigarette is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lowlife cadges a fag-end to puff on.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure meat or fish is to preserve it, which may be done by smoking it.

clue.text: The virtue I display causes surprised comment

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of their virtue draws gasps.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is the virtue belonging to me; as a phrase it is an exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: Companion takes tea with the president

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Juan Peron was president of Argentina

explanation.surface: A companion has tea with a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an escort who accompanies a young person.

clue.text: Wander around and come by an ingenious device

parts.note: to gad about is to wander in search of pleasure
come by means obtain, or get

explanation.surface: A wanderer happens upon a clever invention.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small clever mechanical contrivance.
